claims.text: Quaternary and ternary subsets of CrMnFeCoNi have short-range compositional ordering or local chemical inhomogeneities that differ from the quinary baseline.
Short-range ordering and local chemical inhomogeneities alter stacking-fault energy relative to the quinary baseline.
Changes in stacking-fault energy alter the balance among dislocation slip, twinning, and martensitic or hcp transformation.
Distinct mechanical behavior among these alloys cannot be explained by constituent count alone.
The compared quinary, quaternary, and ternary alloys can all be prepared as single-phase FCC materials with comparable grain sizes and microstructures.
All alloys will undergo identical thermomechanical processing.

In-situ synchrotron or neutron diffraction combined with atom-probe tomography and TEM can quantify the presence and evolution of short-range order or local compositional fluctuations during deformation.
The alloys will be compared at the same temperature, strain rate, sample geometry, processing history, and mechanical loading conditions.
Short-range ordering and local chemical fluctuations affect lattice distortion and stacking-fault energy.
In CoCrNi, short-range order raises barriers to dislocation activity and can increase strength.
Local ordering modulates fault energies across the CrMnFeCoNi subsets.
Local ordering can amplify or suppress twinning and stacking-fault formation during deformation.
Changes in defect activity caused by local ordering change flow stress, work hardening, and fracture mode.
Subsets with stronger local ordering will have lower stacking-fault energy.
Lower stacking-fault energy promotes planar slip, twinning, stacking faults, or phase transformation.
Subsets with stronger ordering will show higher work-hardening rates and altered strength-ductility combinations relative to quinary CrMnFeCoNi.
Equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi is an established single-phase FCC reference alloy.
Equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi has an intermediate stacking-fault energy.
The hypothesis is restricted to alloys retaining a single-phase FCC matrix before deformation, with comparable grain sizes and identical test conditions.
A lack of significant ordering or compositional-fluctuation differences despite persistent mechanical differences would falsify ordering as the primary explanation.
